title: 26 hydrate-named records map to anhydrous terms; 10 terms absorb multiple distinct hydrates
body:
## The check

Flag any record whose `preferred_term` names a hydrate (`x n H2O`, `·nH2O`,
`hydrate`) while its recorded formula/SMILES/InChI contain **no water
component**. Purely mechanical.

**Result: 26 records.**

## Why the existing CAS-vs-structure check cannot see this

Both compared fields are populated from the same ChEBI term by
`AUTO_BACKFILL_CHEBI_CHEMISTRY`, so they agree **by construction**. The check
compares the record against itself; the *label* is the only field carrying the
contradicting information, and nothing was comparing against it.

## The sharper pattern: one term absorbing many distinct hydrates

**10 ontology terms carry 26 distinct hydrate labels between them:**

| term | absorbs |
|---|---|
| CHEBI:34683 | `Na2HPO4 x 2/3/6/7/12 H2O` — **five** different hydrates |
| CHEBI:35696 | `CoCl2 x 2/4/6 H2O` |
| CHEBI:34887 | `NiCl2 x 2/5/6 H2O` |
| CHEBI:75832 | `FeSO4 x 5/6/7 H2O` |
| CHEBI:23414 | `CuSO4 x 2/4 H2O` |
| CHEBI:30812 | `FeCl2 x 6/7 H2O` |
| CHEBI:86360 | `MnSO4 x 1/7 H2O` |
| CHEBI:53001 | `NiSO4 x 6/7 H2O` |

Different hydrates are different substances with different formula weights and
different CAS numbers. Collapsed onto one term they are indistinguishable
downstream — a recipe calling for the heptahydrate and one calling for the
dihydrate become the same node.

**The assignment is demonstrably arbitrary.** Magnesium sulfate splits across two
terms *by notation rather than by chemistry*:

```
CHEBI:32599  <- "MgSO4 x 6 H2O",  "MgSO4·7H2O"
CHEBI:31795  <- "MgSO4 x 7 H2O",  "MgSO4·H2O"
```

The **same** hydration number (7) lands on two different terms depending on
whether the label was written `x 7 H2O` or `·7H2O`. That is lexical matching
with no chemistry behind it.

One record states the contradiction outright: `Na2-EDTA x 2 H2O` carries
`ontology_label: EDTA disodium salt (anhydrous)`.

## Triage forks three ways — do not mass-apply

Established from three worked cases:

1. **The label is wrong.** `CaSO4 x 7 H2O` — no calcium sulfate heptahydrate
   exists (ChEBI has anhydrous/hemi/dihydrate only). Probably a `2`→`7` slip,
   but confirming needs the source recipes read. MediaDive maps
   `CaSO4 x 2 H2O` correctly, so it does distinguish these when they are real.
2. **The label is right and the ontology is deficient.** `CeCl3 x 7 H2O` is the
   standard commercial form; ChEBI has **no** cerium chloride hydrate at all.
   Ignoring the waters here is a **51% formula-weight error** (246 → 373).
   Candidate for a registry term.
3. **Neither side is definite.** `Cefsulodin sodium salt hydrate` — no hydrate
   term in any ontology *and* the label states no hydration number. Nothing to
   encode; the fix is dropping `EXACT_MATCH` and recording why.

So a lexical `x n H2O` sweep would fix (1) and corrupt (2).

## Suggested action

Add the detector as a standing check, then triage the 26 by the fork above.
The `Na2HPO4` five-way and `CoCl2`/`NiCl2` three-way collapses are the highest
value — they are the cases where distinct media ingredients have become
indistinguishable.

## Provenance

Detector proposed by the Claude research lane after the CAS-vs-structure check
passed on three defective records in one batch, with the correct diagnosis of
why it structurally could not catch them. Verified repo-wide.
Related: #315, #317, #320.
